newsitem.title: USA: Oncogene, Cold Spring, Roche form new firm.
newsitem.headline: Oncogene, Cold Spring, Roche form new firm.

text.p: Oncogene Science Inc, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and affiliates of Roche Holding Ltd said Thursday they had signed collaborative pacts and formed a new company, Helicon Therapeutics Inc.
The company will discover, develop, and commercialize novel drugs to treat long-term memory disorders and other central nervous system dysfunctions, the group said.
The pacts call for Oncogene Science to contribute assay biology, high throughput screening and lead optimization.

Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory will contribute scientific research in long-term memory and central nerve system disorders and Roche will provide research funding, a capital contribution and expertise in nerve research, molecular biology, advanced chemistry and product development.

"This is an ideal discovery and development partnership in the central nervous system area, combining Oncogene Science's proven capabilities in drug discovery, Roche's expertise in CNS research and drug development and Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory's cutting-edge genetic research," Cold Spring Harbor James Watson said.

The group said Walter Lovenberg, a former executive vice president of Marion Merrell Dow Inc, has been named chief executive of their company. Lovenberg was also president of Marion Merrell's Research Institute from 1989 to 1993.
Oncogene, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and laboratory scientists and others at the Laboratory and Roche will each have a significant, but not a controlling interest in the new company.
